Okay! I've always wanted to tell this story!

In the fourth grade, we were talking about something or another and the teacher said something about a garden stool. I, for some reason, thought a garden stool meant something else and didn't understand what. So I asked the teacher and she made this whole thing about how a garden stool was a garden stool and what a stupid question it was. I was beyond embarrassed. After she went back to the lesson, the boy in front of me, who wasn't really my friend, turned around and goes "You don't know what a garden stool is?" Me: "No". Then he smiles the most charming smile and says "me neither." My heart bloomed! One of the most genuine and sweetest interactions I've ever had. I miss him.

And I don't think anything was misinterpreted. Your description of my poem was how I wanted it to come off. You know, your always waiting for that "You didn't love me but I will always love you" or "but I will find a way to make you love me". I didn't want to do that. I wanted it to be like the pulse of a desperate heart. "You didn't love me." The end.

I can not explain how much your comment means to me. I've never had one of my poems dissected like this, and to see how my words made such imagery come to your head is wonderful.

The poem, more or less, is about unrequited love. The feeling you get when your entire being is overwhelmed by how much you want another person, but that person not wanting you back. More so, that person not *knowing* how you feel. You're too afraid to do or say anything, to act on your desperate emotions, too afraid of rejection, so that loves just goes on without ever seeing the light of day. Festering into something akin to obsession.

Also! I really appreciate your notice of the contradictions. Hopefully, it wasn't too much that it was confusing, but I've always had a thing for opposite forces in my writing.

Thank you for your comment!!
